task.description: Rework of REQ-202's Step 2a implementation per TEST-DESIGNER's step-03 findings (defect_a_duplicate_index_name and defect_b_truncated_constraint_name_mismatch): the migration's unique_index/3 and index/3 on artifact_versions both defaulted to the same Ecto-generated 66-byte index name (collides AND exceeds Postgres's 63-byte NAMEDATALEN limit, so Postgres silently truncates it), and ArtifactVersion.changeset/2's unique_constraint/3 referenced the full untruncated name, never matching the real (truncated) constraint Postgres raises against -- breaking design section 4.4's concurrency-retry contract.
acceptance_criteria: The migration gives both the unique_index/3 and the index/3 call on artifact_versions explicit, distinct, well-under-63-byte names via the :name option
ArtifactVersion.changeset/2's unique_constraint/3 :name option exactly matches the migration's new explicit unique index name
Any other unique/FK constraint name introduced by this migration is audited for the same length/collision risk
test/letflow/repository_test.exs and test/letflow/repository/canonicaliser_test.exs pass against real Postgres
mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix format --check-formatted both pass

result.summary: Fixed both defects TEST-DESIGNER found by actually running the suite against real Postgres. (1) priv/repo/migrations/20260830030001_create_repository_artifacts.exs: gave unique_index/3 the explicit name :artifact_versions_kind_name_number_idx and the plain index/3 (desc: :version_number) the explicit name :artifact_versions_kind_name_number_desc_idx -- both short, distinct, and well under the 63-byte NAMEDATALEN limit, eliminating both the name collision and the silent-truncation risk. Added a migration comment explaining why (Ecto's default-index-naming strips desc: annotations, so both calls previously generated the identical 66-byte name). (2) lib/letflow/repository/artifact_version.ex: changed @unique_version_number_constraint_name from the old 66-byte default-derived atom to :artifact_versions_kind_name_number_idx, exactly matching the migration's new explicit unique index name, so unique_constraint/3's error-catching now actually matches the real Postgres constraint name and design section 4.4's concurrency-retry contract fires correctly. Audited every other unique/FK constraint this migration introduces for the same risk: repository_artifacts primary key (content_hash, no derived name), artifact_versions_content_hash_fkey (35 bytes), artifact_versions_parent_version_id_fkey (40 bytes), artifact_versions_content_hash_index (36 bytes) -- all well under 63 bytes, none at risk, no further changes needed.
files_modified: priv/repo/migrations/20260830030001_create_repository_artifacts.exs (added explicit :name options to unique_index/3 and index/3 on artifact_versions, plus an explanatory comment)
lib/letflow/repository/artifact_version.ex (@unique_version_number_constraint_name updated to match the migration's new explicit unique index name, plus an explanatory comment)
